newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Goodwill plans Singapore packaging IPO.
newsitem.headline: Goodwill plans Singapore packaging IPO.

text.p: Goodwill Investment (Holdings) Ltd said it had applied to list its packaging business on the foreign board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore through a public offering and placement of Winbox Holdings Pte Ltd shares.
The company said in a statement on Friday that Winbox would hold Goodwill's packaging business following a corporate restructuring.
The share offering would comprise new Winbox shares and part of the shares held by certain shareholders, including Goodwill, and represent up to 40 percent of Winbox's enlarged issued share capital.
The size of the share offering, price and timing will be fixed after the application for listing has been approved in principle by the Singapore stock exchange, Goodwill said.
Its stake would be cut to about 44.9 percent of Winbox's enlarged share capital compared with a current 74.1 percent.
Winbox is mainly engaged in the design, manufacture, sale and distribution of packaging products for luxury consumer goods.
Combined profit after tax and minority interests attributable to Winbox for the year ended March 31, 1996, was about HK$21.9 million.
Net proceeds from the issue of new Winbox shares would be used to finance expansion of the packaging business and finance investments or acquisitions in China.

"The proposed listing of Winbox will strengthen both the financial as well as the marketing positions of the company and Winbox to pursue the China business packaging concept," Goodwill said. "The directors believe that...there will be an improvement in earnings of Winbox in the long term as a result of its expansion, which will offset any potential dilution effect on the group due to the decrease in the group's attributable interest in Winbox," it added.

It said it would "continue to focus on its three core businesses which are the provision of financial services, direct investments and property development and investment" and use part of the proceeds from the sale of its Winbox shares to develop and expand its business.
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp Ltd has been appointed manager of the offer. Goodwill said it did not intend to offer Winbox shares to existing shareholders.
Goodwill shares closed at HK$3.35 on Thursday.
